```{r setup, message=FALSE}
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(purrr)
library(readr)
library(tidyr)
```

## Problem 1

I represented birthdays using the numbers 1 through 365. Then I sampled with
replacement so that more than one person could be born on the same day.

```{r}
set.seed(8105)

shared_birthday = function(group_size) {
  birthdays = sample(1:365, size = group_size, replace = TRUE)
  any(duplicated(birthdays))
}

birthday_sim =
  expand_grid(
    group_size = 2:50,
    iter = 1:10000
  ) |>
  mutate(
    shared = map(group_size, shared_birthday)
  ) |>
  unnest(shared)
```

Each row represents one simulated group. I averaged the TRUE/FALSE results
within each group size to estimate the probability of a shared birthday.

```{r prob}
birthday_prob =
  birthday_sim |>
  group_by(group_size) |>
  summarize(probability = mean(shared))
```

```{r plot, fig.width=7, fig.height=4}
birthday_prob |>
  ggplot(aes(x = group_size, y = probability)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point(size = 1.5) +
  labs(
    title = "How likely is a shared birthday?",
    x = "Number of people",
    y = "Estimated probability"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12)
```

With just 23 people, the chance of a shared birthday was already about 52%.
It reached about 97% with 50 people. As the group gets larger, there are
more pairs of people who could share a birthday.
